newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Defence chief sees no new military bloc for Russia.
newsitem.headline: Defence chief sees no new military bloc for Russia.

text.p: Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov said on Thursday that Moscow remained firmly opposed to NATO's plans to expand eastwards but did not plan to respond by creating its own new military bloc.

"If NATO wants to expand let it expand, but we are against this," Rodionov told a news conference. "For our part we are not going to expand and it does not seem we are going to set up any new military bloc."

President Boris Yeltsin, who is now in hospital recovering from pneumonia, reiterated Moscow's tough opposition to the planned expansion last week and ordered his government to work out countersteps should the enlargement take place.
Rodionov, 60, is a career officer who became Russia's first civilian defence minister after leaving active military service.

Asked whether he saw the possibility of forming a military alliance with Belarus, the former Soviet republic whose leaders and population have expressed interest in strengthening ties with Russia, Rodionov replied: "For the time being I am against any defence alliance."
"But this is for the supreme political leadership to decide," he added.
Rodionov said his ministry monitored potential military threats to Russia's national security from various directions, including the West.
But he said this was normal for any defence ministry and did not mean he viewed any specific country as an immediate foe.
"Russia faces potential threats from the west, south and east," he said replying to the question whether he saw NATO's expansion as a threat to Russia. "But these are potential threats, not enemies."

NATO, which is expected to make a final decision later this year on admitting some of Moscow's Cold War allies as full members, is trying to ease Russia's fears that such moves will threaten its security.
NATO Secretary General Javier Solana is due to hold talks Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov in Moscow on Monday.
